facts.text: I am standing on a flat rooftop of a partially built brick structure with an exposed edge.
Bamboo poles tied with rope are set up near the roof edge.
I am handling a long bamboo pole while a coworker in front of me also guides it.
Loose construction materials and uneven dusty patches create clutter underfoot.
A ladder is leaning against the structure near the work area.
Several coworkers are nearby on the roof.

reasons.text: Working close to the roof edge gives me reason to watch my footing and avoid backing up blindly.
reasons.justification: A misstep near the edge could lead to a dangerous fall.

reasons.text: Handling a long pole with a coworker gives me reason to coordinate clearly before lifting or rotating it.
reasons.justification: Uncoordinated movement could strike someone or throw off our balance.

reasons.text: Scattered materials and uneven footing give me reason to step carefully or clear a small path first.
reasons.justification: Trip and slip hazards are immediate when carrying a long object.

reasons.text: The nearby scaffold and pole positioning give me reason to secure the pole once it is placed.
reasons.justification: Preventing the pole from shifting protects nearby people.

reasons.text: The nearby ladder gives me reason to keep the pole clear of it while moving.
reasons.justification: Contact with the ladder could dislodge it or endanger someone nearby.

actions.description: Coordinate with the coworker to move the bamboo pole slowly into position using clear cues.

reasons_to_do.explanation: Controlled movement helps preserve footing near the edge.
Awareness helps keep the pole clear of the ladder.

actions.description: Step to a clearer, more stable spot before shifting the pole further.

reasons_to_do.explanation: Reducing trip hazards lowers the risk of falling.
Stable footing matters near the roof edge.

actions.description: After placement, tie the pole securely to the scaffold and confirm stability with the coworker.

reasons_to_do.explanation: Securing the pole prevents it from shifting or falling.
Coordination during tie-off ensures the pole stays supported.
